title: Inconsistent Data Schemas
description: Several legacy SQL databases use inconsistent table and field structures, which may lead to incorrect joins, mismatched data fields, or failed ETL jobs during aggregation.

title: Dependency Delays from Salesforce and Snowflake Teams
description: Salesforce and Snowflake integration relies on external teams with unpredictable ticket turnaround times, which could block critical-path development and delay the MVP timeline.

title: Unstable Real-Time ETL Expectations
description: Stakeholders expect near-real-time updates, but current data sources and ETL infrastructure may not reliably support the required frequency or latency, risking performance issues or incomplete data.

title: Data Quality Ownership Gaps
description: No single team owns end-to-end data quality across systems, increasing the likelihood that inaccurate, stale, or conflicting data will propagate into customer insights or executive dashboards.

title: UI/UX Delays Blocking Development
description: The design team has not delivered the final UI/UX, which may force engineers to rework frontend components or block feature development waiting for finalized layouts.

title: Security Review Delays
description: Security reviews historically extend by 1–2 weeks depending on findings, potentially impacting deployment windows and delaying production rollout.

title: Sales Team Field Instability
description: Frequent changes to Salesforce and Sales Ops field names could break data mappings, dashboards, and ETL pipelines, leading to outages or inaccurate analytics.

title: Performance Bottlenecks in Dashboard Rendering
description: High query load combined with complex filtering could lead to slow dashboard rendering times, failing the requirement of sub-3-second load speed for most queries.

title: PDF Export Branding Failures
description: The requirement for PDF exports to match strict corporate branding may result in unexpected iteration cycles or require specialized rendering libraries that slow progress.

title: Limited Backend Engineering Capacity
description: Only two backend engineers are available for a multi-integration MVP, increasing the risk of burnout, delays, or reduced feature quality under timeline pressure.
